business_problem: Philips needed granular visibility and accountability for technology spending across decentralized systems and a rapidly growing cloud footprint, but existing reporting was manual, lagging and too fragmented to support fact-based optimization.
solution_summary: Philips adopted IBM Apptio and IBM Cloudability as the foundation of a stepwise IT financial management and FinOps transformation. Cloudability delivered real-time visibility into cloud consumption and cost data so teams could move from retrospective reporting to proactive optimization. Around that, Philips established a FinOps operating model with a dedicated TBM Office responsible for governance, data quality and adoption. As the program matured, Apptio was extended beyond cloud-spend analysis into IT service catalog improvements, total-cost-of-ownership modeling, showback, planning and forecasting. The implementation harmonized data models from decentralized systems into a single trusted source of truth and replaced spreadsheet-heavy planning with a standardized cadence for investment and optimization decisions. This turned IT cost management from a centralized bookkeeping exercise into a business-facing operating system for transparency, forecasting and continuous savings.

solution_components.name: IBM Apptio
solution_components.role: Provides the planning, TCO, showback and broader IT financial management foundation for Philips' TBM operating model.

solution_components.name: IBM Cloudability
solution_components.role: Supplies real-time cloud-spend visibility, commitments insight and optimization recommendations for the FinOps workflow.

data_flow: Technology cost and cloud-consumption data from decentralized systems flows into Cloudability and Apptio, where it is normalized for visibility, TCO modeling, forecasting and showback before being surfaced to finance, IT and business stakeholders for optimization decisions.
business_outcome: Philips achieved measurable cloud savings in the first year, accelerated planning and reporting cycles and gave business, finance and IT leaders a shared fact base for ongoing optimization instead of spreadsheet-driven reconciliation.
metrics: 10% cloud cost savings achieved in the first year
100% allocation and real time visibility of cloud consumption
architecture_clues: A dedicated TBM Office owns governance, data quality and adoption as the program scales.
Philips deliberately started with FinOps before expanding into broader TBM capabilities.
The implementation harmonized decentralized cost models into a single source of truth.
